why: Hybrid anchoring: enter by meaning, leave by typed edge. The anchor is CLASS-QUALIFIED because a hop's verdict depends on the source class's `edge_policy` — a bare anchor could not be typechecked before it ran, since the source class would be whatever retrieval returned. It is an ENTRY: only the first step may carry one. It is LOCAL: unlike `retrieve`, it MUST NOT enter through an installed dependency's node, because this response says `"scope": "local"`. And it degrades and says so — this corpus ships no index, so `degraded` is true and `degraded_reason` is `no_index` under the same precedence `retrieve` follows. No score is asserted: a score is a property of a model, and a contract pinning one fails every server that legitimately embeds differently.
